source: Dallas City Code ch. 51P, Article 977 (City Attorney's codified article, April 2026)

sections.title: Legislative History
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.101. LEGISLATIVE HISTORY.

PD 977 was established by Ordinance No. 30275, passed by the Dallas City Council on December 14, 2016. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Property Location And Size
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.102. PROPERTY LOCATION AND SIZE.

PD 977 is established on property located on the south line of Walnut Hill Lane, east of Mixon Drive. The size of PD 977 is approximately 0.896 acre. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Definitions And Interpretations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.103. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS.

(a) Unless otherwise stated, the definitions and interpretations in Chapter 51A apply to this article. In this district:

(1) FACADE WALL means any separate face of a building, including parapet walls and omitted wall lines, or any part of a building that encloses usable space. Where separate faces are oriented in the same direction, or in the directions within 45 degrees of one another, they are considered as part of a single facade wall.

(2) PRIMARY FACADE WALL means the facade wall containing the primary entrance. If two or more facades walls have entrances of equal significance, each facade wall will be considered a primary facade wall.

(3) REAR FACADE WALL means the facade wall containing service areas.

(4) SERVICE AREA means any area for loading docks, outdoor storage (other than an outdoor display, sales, and storage area), trash collection or compaction, truck parking, or other similar functions.

(5) SIDE FACADE WALL means any facade wall that is not a primary facade wall or a rear facade wall.

(b) Unless otherwise stated, all references to articles, divisions, or sections in this article are to articles, divisions, or sections in Chapter 51A.

(c) This district is considered to be a residential zoning district. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Exhibit
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.104. EXHIBIT.

The following exhibit is incorporated into this article: Exhibit 977A: development plan. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Development Plan
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.105. DEVELOPMENT PLAN.

Development and use of the Property must comply with the development plan (Exhibit 977A). If there is a conflict between the text of this article and the development plan, the text of this article controls. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Main Uses Permitted
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.106. MAIN USES PERMITTED.

The following use is the only main use permitted:

-- Local utilities. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Accessory Uses
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.107. ACCESSORY USES.

As a general rule, an accessory use is permitted in any district in which the main use is permitted. Some specific accessory uses, however, due to their unique nature, are subject to additional regulations in Section 51A-4.217. For more information regarding accessory uses, consult Section 51A-4.217. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Yard, Lot, And Space Regulations
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.108. YARD, LOT, AND SPACE REGULATIONS.

(Note: The yard, lot, and space regulations in this section must be read together with the yard, lot, and space regulations in Division 51A-4.400. If there is a conflict between this section and Division 51A-4.400, this section controls.)

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, the yard, lot, and space regulations for the R-10(A) Single Family District apply.

(b) Stories. Maximum number of stories above grade is one. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Off-Street Parking And Loading
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.109. OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING.

Consult the use regulations in Division 51A-4.200 for the specific off-street parking and loading requirements for each use. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Environmental Performance Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.110. ENVIRONMENTAL PERFORMANCE STANDARDS.

See Article VI. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Design Standards
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.111. DESIGN STANDARDS.

(a) Purpose. These design standards are intended to ensure the pump station is compatible with the surrounding area and mitigate the negative impact, while allowing creativity, flexibility, and variety in design. Building massing and height must take into consideration the height and scale of neighboring structures and provide architectural features that address adjacent buildings.

(b) Facade walls. Primary facade walls and side facade walls must incorporate at least three of the following design elements. Rear facade walls must incorporate at least two of the following design elements. The cumulative length of these design elements must extend for at least 60 percent of the facade wall’s horizontal length.

(1) A repeating pattern of wall recesses and projections, such as bays, offsets, reveals, or projecting ribs, that have a relief of at least eight inches.

(2) At least one of the following design elements at the primary entrance, so that the primary entrance is architecturally prominent:

(A) Architectural details such as arches, friezes, tile work, murals, or moldings.

(B) Integral planters or wing walls that incorporate landscaping or seating.

(C) Enhanced exterior light fixtures such as wall sconces, light coves with concealed light sources, ground-mounted accent lights, or decorative pedestal lights.

(D) Prominent three-dimensional features, such as chimneys, domes, spires, towers, or turrets.

(E) A repeating pattern of pilasters projecting from the facade wall by a minimum of eight inches or architectural or decorative columns.

(3) Arcades, awnings, canopies, covered walkways, or porticos.

(4) Trim or accent elements using decorative contrasting colors of at least 10 percent of the area of the facade wall exclusive of fenestration.

(c) Materials and colors. No more than 75 percent of the area of a facade may have a single material or color.

(d) Roofs.

(1) Roof-mounted mechanical equipment must be screened or set back so that they are not visible from a point five feet, six inches above grade at the property line. Screening materials must match the materials and colors used on the main building and be integral with the design of the overall facade. Chain link fence may not be used as a screening material.

(2) Roof lines visible from the right-of-way or residential property must be segmented and provide a minimum of three elevation heights.

(3) Roofs must have at least one of the following design elements:

(A) Parapets with detailing such as cornices, moldings, trim, or variations in brick coursing.

(B) Sloping roofs with at least two of the following design elements:

(i) Slope of at least 5:12.

(ii) Two or more slope planes.

(iii) Overhanging eaves extending at least three feet beyond the supporting wall.

(e) Mechanical equipment on the ground. Mechanical equipment on the ground must be screened using materials matching the materials and colors used on the main building. Chain link fence may not be used as a screening material. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Landscaping
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.112. LANDSCAPING.

(a) In general. Except as provided in this section, landscaping must be provided in accordance with Article X.

(b) Street buffer. Except as provided in this subsection, landscaping in the front yard must include a street buffer, as described in Section 51A-10.126.

(1) The street buffer must have a depth no less than 30 feet from the property line that defines the front yard.
(2) The street buffer must incorporate no less than three buffer plant groups.

(A) Two buffer plant groups must be located within 20 feet of the building foundation.

(B) Each buffer plant group must consist of one large canopy tree, two small ornamental trees, and planting beds consisting of a mix of the following landscape materials:

(i) Shrubs.

(ii) Ornamental grasses.

(iii) Groundcover.

(iv) Aggregates.

(v) Boulders.

(C) Shrubs must be a minimum 36 inches in height at the time of planting and have a minimum mature height of six feet.

(D) Tree species must be selected from the list of approved replacement trees in Section 51A-10.134.

(E) Trees must have a minimum caliper of two inches at time of planting.

(F) Tree drip lines (at maturity) must not be located within 10 feet of a water transmission line.

(G) Shrubs must not be planted within five feet of a water transmission line.

(c) Open spaces. Open spaces must be covered with turf grass, aggregate, or permanent paving material.

(d) Maintenance. Plant materials must be maintained in a healthy, growing condition. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Signs
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.113. SIGNS.

Signs must comply with the provisions for non-business zoning districts in Article VII and the attached development plan. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Additional Provisions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.114. ADDITIONAL PROVISIONS.

(a) Fencing must be constructed of wrought iron or a similar decorative metal along street and neighboring property frontages. Along alley frontages, the fence may be constructed of

chain-link and barbed wire. A fence with a maximum height of eight feet is permitted in the front yard.

(b) The Property must be properly maintained in a state of good repair and neat appearance.

(c) Development and use of the Property must comply with all federal and state laws and regulations, and with all ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 30275)

sections.title: Compliance With Conditions
sections.text:
SEC. 51P-977.115. COMPLIANCE WITH CONDITIONS.

(a) All paved areas, permanent drives, streets, and drainage structures, if any, must be constructed in accordance with standard city specifications, and completed to the satisfaction of the city.

(b) The building official shall not issue a building permit to authorize work, or a certificate of occupancy to authorize the operation of a use, until there has been full compliance with this article, the Dallas Development Code, the construction codes, and all other ordinances, rules, and regulations of the city. (Ord. 30275)
